text:
jamie: quick check — do our app logs redact Authorization headers and any model prompts that might contain PII? saw this in staging logs:
```
POST /v1/generate 200
headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer sk-abc123xyz", "Content-Type":"application/json" }
body: { "prompt": "User email: alice@example.com\nQuestion: how do I reset my password?" }
```
Can't tell if logstash is removing tokens from body or just headers. @saira @matt

saira: short answer: headers are stripped by ingest (we gsub Authorization) but bodies are NOT automatically redacted. apps should avoid logging full request bodies or must sanitize prompts before emitting. see internal policy (security/logging) but tl;dr — treat prompts as potential PII. If you need raw logs for debugging, open a one-time access request with justification and trace_ids.

matt: quick add: we run this on ingest for headers:
```
filter {
  if [headers][authorization] {
    mutate { gsub => ["[headers][authorization]", "(?i)Bearer\s+\S+", "REDACTED"] }
  }
}
```
it doesn't touch [body]. we *can* add a mutate gsub for body (e.g., drop prompt keys) but that has perf and parsing risks. preferred: app-level middleware to scrub keys like authorization, access_token, prompt, email before logging.

jamie: ok — I'll open a small middleware PR to redact keys (Authorization, access_token, prompt, user_email) before any log.info calls. also will clip large bodies >1KB. pinging for review.

saira: SGTM. For one-time raw log access we need: reason + trace_id(s) + time window + list of reviewers. infra will grant max 24h window. Please put requests in infra-requests and tag @infra-oncall.

sec-bot: Automated note: access requests for raw logs require approval from infra (infra-logs-access) and audit logging will record reviewers.

jamie: thanks. one more Q: confirm we should mask prompts in telemetry/metrics too (we currently send prompt length and success flags but not content) — want to avoid accidental storage of PII in eval/telemetry.

saira: correct — telemetry must only contain aggregated metrics and non-identifying metadata. if you need to store prompts for evals, use the sanitized eval pipeline (opt-in) or store hashed tokens only. see policy section 4 for examples.

matt: if helpful I can add an ELK ingest rule to drop body fields named "prompt" entirely for staging + dev to be safe while you ship the middleware. want me to do that?

jamie: please do for staging. will follow up with the PR link and trace_ids once ready. thx!
